transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, the main thing that pushed me to come in is work. I process insurance claims, and I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews, I keep leaving my desk. It's just getting to be a real problem for me.
When you get up from your desk, is it because you feel you have to do it to relieve a thought or urge that keeps bothering you?

No, it's not really like that. I don't have any specific thoughts or urges bothering me that I'm trying to get rid of. It's more just... I get restless, I guess? Or I just find myself getting up without really thinking about it. It's not to relieve anything specific like that.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic compared with your normal self?
No, I don't think so. I haven't really had any times where I felt way more energetic than usual. I just feel like my normal self, really.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks, like losing track of what you’re doing or getting distracted easily?

Yeah, definitely. It happens a lot at work. If the people near me start talking about a different claim, or even if I just suddenly remember some random errand I need to run, my attention just completely slides off what I'm doing. I end up having to reread the same section of a claim a few times because I just wasn't taking it in.
Looking back to when you were a child, did you often have the same kind of trouble staying focused or sitting still?

Yeah, looking back, this isn't really a brand new thing for me. Like, in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but... I was always losing my worksheets. I'd miss instructions a lot, too, and they constantly had to give me reminders just to finish my classwork. So, yeah, I guess I've always kind of struggled with it.
Do these same focus or restlessness problems also cause trouble for you outside of work, like at home or in everyday tasks?

Not really, no. I haven't really noticed it being much of an issue at home. I mean, work is where I really have to sit down and force myself to get through those claims. At home, if I get distracted or wander off to do something else, it doesn't really matter as much. So... no, I can't really think of any major trouble it causes outside of my job.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?

No, I don't really think so. I mean, I get stressed sometimes if I'm falling behind on my claims at work, but I wouldn't say I'm a worrier in general. If there's nothing going on, I'm usually pretty relaxed. I don't just sit around worrying about things for no reason.
